## Cotopaxi National Park

What a breathtaking sight: snowcapped Cotopaxi Volcano! Its almost perfect cone rises above the horizon like a guardian of ancient legends. At dawn, when the first rays of sunlight paint Cotopaxi's snowy slopes in shades of gold, the volcano comes alive like a majestic work of nature.

You will head south along the Pan-American Highway toward Cotopaxi Volcano. At 5,897 meters, it is Ecuador's second-highest peak. Cotopaxi is active and easily recognized by its snow-covered conical shape. It is surrounded by the beautiful vegetation of the high Andes.

The excursion begins with visitor registration at the southern entrance to the national park. We will then visit the interpretation center to learn about the area's flora and fauna, the volcano and the Andes mountain range. Afterwards, we will take a one-hour walk around Limpiopungo Lagoon, an excellent place to admire the majestic volcano and take beautiful photographs, weather permitting.

Optionally, you can travel by car to the parking area for José Rivas Mountain Refuge. From there, a 200-meter walk leads to the refuge, which stands directly below the glacier and serves as a base for climbers ascending the volcano's summit. Please note that the parking area is at an altitude of 4,600 meters.

## Cotopaxi — the Heart of Ecuador

Cotopaxi is a majestic volcano whose snow-covered summit seems to crown the sky, inspiring awe with its enduring strength and natural grandeur. To climb the slopes of Cotopaxi is to touch something timeless, where every step reveals panoramas of boundless plains and rugged mountain scenery.

You will see everyday life in La Paz, its colonial architecture and political center. The route ends at the Killi Killi viewpoint.

First, you will explore the traditional markets of La Paz, which sell food, textiles and handicrafts. Along the way, the route passes San Pedro Prison. You will then take a ride on the city's cable-car transport system, with panoramic views of La Paz and the surrounding Andes.

In the historic center, you will visit the Witches' Market, associated with Andean beliefs, spiritual practices and offerings to Pachamama. The route then takes you past San Francisco Church and Murillo Square, home to the Government Palace, the Legislative Palace and the Metropolitan Cathedral.

The final stop is the Killi Killi viewpoint, offering a 360-degree panorama of the city. Departure from the hotel is scheduled for 9:00.

The excursion begins with departure from the hotel at 08:00. From La Paz, you will travel to Tiwanaku, one of the region's most important pre-Inca archaeological complexes. In December 2000, Tiwanaku was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. On the way, you will enjoy views of the Cordillera Real of the Andes, snowcapped peaks and the broad valleys of the Altiplano.

## The Rich Heritage of Tiwanaku

Your introduction to Tiwanaku begins at the Lithic and Ceramic Museums. Exhibits include pottery, stone monoliths and other finds associated with the Tiwanaku civilization, which flourished from approximately AD 300 to 1000.

Next, you will visit the complex's principal monuments: the Akapana Pyramid, the Semi-Subterranean Temple, the Kalasasaya Temple, the Ponce Monolith and the Gate of the Sun. Carved stone heads survive in the Semi-Subterranean Temple, while the Gate of the Sun is decorated with intricate carvings and images connected with Tiwanaku religious beliefs.

After exploring the complex, the route continues to Desaguadero on the border between Bolivia and Peru. On arrival, a Peruvian guide will meet you for the continuation of your journey on the Peruvian side.

The guided excursion introduces La Paz and its Witches' Market, where traditional Andean remedies and ritual objects are sold.

You will then visit Moon Valley on the outskirts of the city. Erosion has created a maze of clay peaks and pale stone pillars here.

The next part of the route explores Tiwanaku, a pre-Columbian archaeological complex approximately 72 km from La Paz. In the “Enchanting Peru and Bolivia” program, the visit is scheduled for the day of the return flight to Lima; the excursion timetable and flight are coordinated at booking.
